# The end message

Open when: finishing any ui-factory run, or stopping at a requested stage. Text for him passes the writing skill's owner surface.

1. State: "usable", "still unfinished" or "ready to ship", in plain words, with the unfinished list. Unfinished parts carry a mark inside the app in development builds.
2. Each item is marked proposed, selected, implemented or verified (verified means a real run was shown, not that a helper said so). A concept image is never called a working interface.
3. What to look at and how: the screen, the state, the URL or command, and the picture pair where the approved image exists.
4. Not stops, shown here: per-screen direction picks by the critique (he can overrule), critique results, break-ui findings that are design decisions, rule or check offers from corrections (yes and no buttons), whole-app findings as picture pairs, and better ways found that he did not ask for, each as a short card (idea, goal it serves, source or "my guess", what it would change, the run that would show it works) with accept, park or reject.
5. Packages installed in his project (for example the Vercel UI SDK) and why.
6. Which Emil skill files were read at which stage (from the run notes). Do not claim a skill ran if its file was not read.
7. Scripts run with their results, and scripts not run with the reason.
8. If no brand stage has run: say the tokens used are candidates marked unconfirmed and the brand stage has not been run.
9. Handoff detail (references, approved and rejected images, brand folder, decision record, screenshots, interaction checks, open issues) lives in `brand/` and the run notes so another agent can continue without reopening settled taste; the message gives one path to it, not the contents.
